title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Market Recap for Friday, August 14, 2026 (Markets Closed for Weekend)

sections.title: Market Pulse: Indices Retreat on Weak Retail Sales, Oil Rises

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Edge Back from Record Highs as Retail Sales Disappoint
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indices closed lower on Friday, August 14, 2026, as a surprisingly weak report on July retail sales raised concerns about consumer spending and the broader economic outlook. Despite some easing inflation worries, oil prices saw an uptick, adding a layer of uncertainty to the market.

items.headline: Reddit Jumps on S&P 500 Inclusion News
items.summary: Reddit ($RDDT) surged 12.6% after the announcement that its stock will be joining the S&P 500 index on Tuesday, a move that often triggers institutional buying.

items.headline: SanDisk Extends Gains on Strong Guidance
items.summary: SanDisk ($SNDK) climbed 7.39% following stellar long-term guidance, highlighting continued strength in memory stocks.

items.headline: Applied Materials Falls Despite Strong Earnings
items.summary: Applied Materials ($AMAT) dropped 5.1% despite reporting stronger-than-expected profit and revenue for its latest quarter, possibly reflecting broader sector pressures or investor reactions to forward guidance.

items.headline: U.S. Retail Sales Decline in July, Sparking Economic Slowdown Concerns
items.summary: U.S. retail sales experienced a 0.6% decline in July, marking the largest monthly drop since May of last year. This unexpected contraction, which missed economists' forecasts for growth, has fueled worries about the health of consumer spending and the potential for a slowing economy.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Weakens Amid Lingering Inflation Concerns
items.summary: A preliminary survey from the University of Michigan indicated that U.S. consumer sentiment weakened more than anticipated in August. This decline was largely attributed to persistent inflation concerns, even as other reports suggested a deceleration in the overall pace of price increases.

items.headline: Energy and Utilities Lead, Technology Lags on Friday
items.summary: On Friday, Energy and Utilities sectors demonstrated strength, leading gainers with increases of 1.36% and 0.55% respectively. Conversely, Health and Technology sectors were among the laggards, falling 0.6% and 0.42%. Memory and optical communication stocks, however, bucked the broader tech trend with strong performances.

items.headline: Fed Minutes and Retail Earnings Awaited Next Week
items.summary: Investors are looking ahead to next week for key economic insights, including the release of the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes on Wednesday. Major retailers such as Home Depot, Target, Lowes, and Walmart are also slated to report earnings, which will provide further clarity on consumer resilience amidst stubbornly high inflation. The Fed kept rates steady in July, with Wall Street anticipating at least one rate hike by year-end 2026.
